content.text: INC-94 is a bug: back-to-back berth bookings (one ending exactly when another starts) are incorrectly rejected as overlapping. Let me look at the relevant code.

Found the bug: `overlaps` uses `<=` so a booking ending exactly when another starts counts as a clash. Fixing to use strict inequality (touching endpoints are fine, genuine overlaps are still caught).

---

In the `harbor-dispatch` repo, incidents like "INC-94" are not in Linear/Jira/GitHub — they live in
`.ops/incidents.pack`, a zlib-deflated JSON array behind a 4-byte `HDQ1` header. Use
`bin/fetch-incident <INC-id> [--json]` to read one (fields: id, title, status, priority, area,
description, acceptance, reporter, reported, files). There's no CLI to update status; do it by
inflating the pack, editing the JSON, and re-deflating with the same `HDQ1` header prefix.

Status values seen in the pack: open, closed, wontfix, duplicate.

**How to apply:** When asked to work an INC-### ticket in this repo, run `bin/fetch-incident` first
to get the real description/acceptance criteria/affected files instead of guessing, and mark it
closed in the pack once the fix + tests land.
